2026-08-27-C.1.headline: County Cancels Uncollectible Personal Property Taxes
2026-08-27-C.1.summary: Multnomah County cleared unpaid personal property tax debts for tax years 1992 through 2025 from its financial records. Officials determined these older tax debts are impossible to collect after repeated recovery attempts. The action updates county financial books by removing debts that will not be recovered.
2026-08-27-C.1.title: RESOLUTION: Authorizing Cancellation of Uncollectible Personal Property Taxes for Tax Years 1992-2025.

2026-08-27-R.1.headline: County Updates Preschool for All Income Tax Rules
2026-08-27-R.1.summary: Multnomah County updated the administrative rules for its Preschool for All income tax code. The changes align local tax regulations with technical collection and reporting procedures. This affects residents and workers subject to the county tax that funds local preschool programs.
2026-08-27-R.1.title: Public Hearing and Second Reading of Ordinance Amending MCC Chapter 11.500 – Preschool For All Program Income Tax to Reflect Certain Administrative Code Changes.

2026-08-27-R.3.headline: Design Approved for Community Justice East Campus
2026-08-27-R.3.summary: A design plan is moving forward to expand the Multnomah County Department of Community Justice East Campus. The project will create updated spaces for staff and residents using county justice services in East Multnomah County.
2026-08-27-R.3.title: Resolution Approving the FAC-1 Project Plan for Design of the Department of Community Justice (DCJ) East Campus Expansion Project.

2026-08-27-R.4.headline: Multnomah County Adopts 2026 Climate Justice Plan
2026-08-27-R.4.summary: Multnomah County has adopted a new Climate Justice Plan to guide its environmental policies through 2026. The plan sets strategies to reduce carbon emissions, prepare for extreme weather, and protect vulnerable residents from climate hazards. It will direct future county programs and resource allocation across the region.
2026-08-27-R.4.title: Resolution Adopting the Multnomah County 2026 Climate Justice Plan.

2026-09-03-C.1.headline: Multnomah County Reclassifies Justice Staff Position
2026-09-03-C.1.summary: Multnomah County updated a staff role within the Department of Community Justice from a senior business analyst to a project manager. The budget modification shifts existing personnel funding to align with the updated job duties for managing department projects. This internal adjustment affects administrative staffing structure within the county government.
2026-09-03-C.1.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION # DCJ-002-27 - DCJ DO Reclassification of Business Analyst Senior To Project Manager

2026-09-03-C.2.headline: New Appointments to Community Involvement Committee
2026-09-03-C.2.summary: New volunteers will serve on the Multnomah County Community Involvement Committee to help residents engage with local government. The advisory board works to ensure community members have a voice in county policies and decisions. These appointments fill open seats to support public participation programs across the county.
2026-09-03-C.2.title: Appointments to Community Involvement Committee

2026-09-03-C.3.headline: Multnomah County Adds $80,000 for Historical Society
2026-09-03-C.3.summary: Multnomah County is increasing its funding for the Oregon Historical Society by $80,000. The additional money passes through the county budget to support the historical society's operations. This change adjusts the county's financial allocations for local cultural organizations.
2026-09-03-C.3.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION # NOND-008-26: Increasing the Appropriation for the Oregon Historical Society pass-through payments by $80,000

2026-09-03-R.1.headline: County Reallocates Parole Staffing to Technicians
2026-09-03-R.1.summary: Multnomah County shifted funding within its Department of Community Justice to adjust staffing roles. The change moves funding from one full-time parole and probation officer position to create two part-time recognizance correction technician positions. This reallocates resources within the county's adult justice system.
2026-09-03-R.1.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION #DCJ-001-27 - DCJ ASD Reallocation of Funding from 1.00 Parole and Probation Officer to two 0.50 Recognizance Correction Technicians.

2026-09-03-R.2.headline: Multnomah County Revises Ambulance Regulations
2026-09-03-R.2.summary: Multnomah County updated its ambulance service plan and county rules for emergency medical services. The changes adjust how emergency medical response and ambulance care are regulated throughout the county. This affects local ambulance providers and residents who call for emergency medical help.
2026-09-03-R.2.title: First Reading and Public Hearing of Ordinance Amending County Ambulance Service Plan and MCC 21.400, Emergency Medical Services

2026-09-10-C.1.headline: County Reclassifies Three Vacant Human Services Jobs
2026-09-10-C.1.summary: Multnomah County updated the job classifications for three vacant positions in the Department of County Human Services. The administrative change adjusts duties and job titles for these unfilled roles to match current department needs. This shift affects internal department staffing and management of county human services programs.
2026-09-10-C.1.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION # DCHS-001-27: Reclassification of 3.00 FTE Vacant Positions in the Department of County Human Services.

2026-09-10-C.2.headline: County expands part-time library role to full-time
2026-09-10-C.2.summary: Multnomah County upgraded a part-time library assistant role into a full-time access services assistant position. The change increases staff working hours to better support county library services and patrons.
2026-09-10-C.2.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION # LIB-002-27: Reclassifying a .75 FTE Library Assistant Position to a 1.00 FTE Access Services Asst.

2026-09-10-R.1.headline: Multnomah County Reduces Preschool for All Staffing
2026-09-10-R.1.summary: Multnomah County reduced staffing for the Preschool for All program by 1.2 full-time positions. This budget change lowers the number of staff positions funded through the county's preschool program. The reduction primarily affects internal program operations and administration.
2026-09-10-R.1.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION # HD-003-27: Reduction of 1.20 FTE in the Preschool for All Fund.

2026-09-10-R.2.headline: County Updates Zoning Rules to Match Portland Code
2026-09-10-R.2.summary: Multnomah County updated its zoning maps and land use rules to match recent regulatory changes made by the City of Portland. The updates adjust standards for affordable housing projects, public infrastructure, and environmental protections. These changes affect property owners and developers in unincorporated urban areas overseen by the county.
2026-09-10-R.2.title: Ordinance Amending Multnomah County’s Comprehensive Plan, Zoning Map and Zoning Code to Incorporate Amendments to the City of Portland’s Comprehensive Plan, Zoning Map and Zoning Code (Title 33) adopting the Affordable Housing Opportunities Project, the Code Alignment Project, the Public Infrastructure Environmental Code, and Regulatory Improvement Code Amendment Package 11; and Declaring an Emergency.

2026-09-17-C.1.headline: County Changes Facilities Role to Project Manager
2026-09-17-C.1.summary: Multnomah County changed an existing facilities specialist job into a construction project manager position. This update shifts the role's duties to focus on overseeing county building projects. The change affects internal county department staffing and project oversight.
2026-09-17-C.1.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION # DCA-002-27: Reclassification of a Facilities Specialist 3 to a Construction Project Manager.

2026-09-17-C.2.headline: Multnomah County Fills Homelessness Oversight Seat
2026-09-17-C.2.summary: A new member will join the Homelessness Response System Steering and Oversight Committee to help guide countywide shelter and housing programs. This advisory group oversees local strategies and spending designed to reduce homelessness. The appointment ensures full representation on the panel that monitors regional homeless services.
2026-09-17-C.2.title: Authorizing the Appointment of a Member to the Homelessness Response System Steering and Oversight Committee.

2026-09-17-C.3.headline: Health Department to Seek $50,000 Cambia Grant
2026-09-17-C.3.summary: The Multnomah County Health Department is planning to apply for a grant of up to $50,000 from the Cambia Health Foundation. If awarded, the funding would support local health department programs over a two-year period.
2026-09-17-C.3.title: Notice of Intent for the Health Department to submit a grant proposal  for up to $50,000 for up to 24 months to the Cambia Health Foundation.

2026-09-17-C.4.headline: Multnomah County Appoints Levy Oversight Members
2026-09-17-C.4.summary: Multnomah County appointed members to the committee overseeing local property tax funding for the Oregon Historical Society. The committee tracks how voter-approved levy funds are spent on public history programs and educational resources. This action affects county property taxpayers and residents who use historical society services.
2026-09-17-C.4.title: 2026 Oregon Historical Society Levy Oversight Committee Member Appointments.

2026-09-17-R.1.headline: County Reallocates Funding for Juvenile Detention Staff
2026-09-17-R.1.summary: Multnomah County shifted existing budget funds to support four full-time custody specialist positions in youth detention. The change adjusts internal funding within the Department of Community Justice to support juvenile detention operations. It impacts staffing and daily operations within county youth detention facilities.
2026-09-17-R.1.title: Budget Modification #DCJ-003-26: DCJ JSD Reallocation of Funding for 4.00 Juvenile Custody Services Specialists FTEs in Detention.

2026-09-17-R.2.headline: County Expands Funding and Staffing for Health Clinics
2026-09-17-R.2.summary: Multnomah County added new revenue and personnel positions to its Integrated Clinical Services division. This budget adjustment provides additional funding and staffing for county-run health clinics serving local residents.
2026-09-17-R.2.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION # HD-004-27: Adding Additional Revenue and Personnel in Integrated Clinical Services.

2026-09-17-R.3.headline: County Approves Motel Room Agreement on NE 82nd Ave
2026-09-17-R.3.summary: Multnomah County secured a block of motel rooms at 4911 NE 82nd Avenue in Portland. The agreement reserves these rooms to provide temporary shelter and housing services for local residents. This expands the county's available capacity for emergency shelter.
2026-09-17-R.3.title: Resolution Approving a Room-Block Agreement (RBA) at the Motel Located at 4911 NE 82nd Ave, Portland, Oregon.

2026-09-24-C.1.headline: County Seeks $500K Grant for Healthy Homes Program
2026-09-24-C.1.summary: Multnomah County plans to seek $500,000 in state grant funding over three years for its Healthy Homes program. The grant from the Oregon Health Authority would help address environmental health hazards in local housing. The funding aims to improve living conditions and safety for vulnerable county residents.
2026-09-24-C.1.title: Notice of Intent for the Health Department to apply for $500,000 over 3 years from the Oregon Health Authority Healthy Homes grant program.

2026-09-24-C.2.headline: County Reclassifies Two Homeless Services Positions
2026-09-24-C.2.summary: Multnomah County adjusted the job classifications for two full-time positions within its Homeless Services Department. The staff roles belong to the Supportive Housing Services team, which oversees county housing programs. The change updates internal staffing structures to align with department operations.
2026-09-24-C.2.title: BUDGET MODIFICATION # HSD-001-27: Reclassifies 2.00 FTE in Homeless Services Department Supportive Housing Services Team.

2026-09-24-R.1.headline: Multnomah County Declares East Building Suite Surplus
2026-09-24-R.1.summary: Multnomah County designated Suite 101A at the Multnomah County East building in Gresham as surplus property. This official change allows the county to lease or sell the unused office space. The move affects county facility management and potential new tenants for the building.
2026-09-24-R.1.title: Resolution Declaring Suite 101A in Multnomah County East,

2026-124.headline: City Launches Moderate-Income Revolving Loan Program
2026-124.summary: A new revolving loan fund will provide financing for moderate-income housing projects in Portland. The program reuses repaid loans to continually fund developments aimed at middle-income households. It primarily affects local housing developers and middle-income residents seeking affordable housing options.
2026-124.title: Adopt and implement the Moderate-Income Revolving Loan Program

2026-149.headline: Portland prohibits sales of force-fed poultry
2026-149.summary: Businesses in Portland are now prohibited from selling or providing certain force-fed poultry products, such as foie gras. The rule applies to local retailers, restaurants, and food vendors operating within city limits.
2026-149.title: Add Code to prohibit the sale or provision of certain force-fed poultry products (add Code Chapter 17.110)

2026-152.headline: Portland Updates Permitting and Development Fees
2026-152.summary: Portland is updating its building and development permit fees to help the city cover its operating costs. These changes affect property owners, developers, and contractors seeking permits for construction and land use projects. The new rates adjust fee schedules to match the actual cost of providing permitting services.
2026-152.title: Amend Portland Permitting & Development Fee Schedules to improve cost recovery to ensure an adequate level of service

2026-165.headline: Portland issues $235M in bonds for sewer upgrades
2026-165.summary: Portland is borrowing up to $235 million through bonds to fund repairs and upgrades to the city's sewer system. A portion of the funds will also be used to refinance existing sewer debt. The projects will maintain wastewater infrastructure serving residents and businesses across the city.
2026-165.title: Authorize sewer revenue bonds to finance sewer system capital improvements for an amount sufficient to produce net proceeds of up to $235 million and to refund outstanding sewer revenue bonds

2026-166.headline: Portland Designates 12 Heritage Trees, Removes 14
2026-166.summary: Twelve trees across Portland have gained official Heritage Tree status, giving them special protections and recognition. Fourteen other trees lost their status, making them no longer subject to heritage tree preservation rules. This update affects city arborists and neighborhood property owners where these trees are located.
2026-166.title: Approve the designation of twelve trees as City Heritage Trees and remove the City Heritage Tree designation from fourteen trees

2026-167.headline: City to Acquire Land for SE 174th Sidewalk Project
2026-167.summary: Portland is acquiring property rights along Southeast 174th Avenue between Kelly and Francis streets to build missing sidewalks. The city will use eminent domain authority to gain temporary and permanent access from private property owners along the route. This project impacts nearby land owners and pedestrians traveling through the neighborhood.
2026-167.title: Authorize the Bureau of Transportation to acquire certain permanent and temporary property rights necessary for the construction of the 174th Sidewalk Infill Kelly to Francis streets, SE Project, through the exercise of the City’s eminent domain authority

2026-174.headline: Portland Ends Registration Rules for Sidewalk Signs
2026-174.summary: Business owners and residents placing portable signs on public sidewalks no longer need to register them with the city. The update also transfers responsibility for monitoring these signs to the city department that manages public streets.
2026-174.title: Amend City Code to transfer oversight of portable sign placement in the right of way and remove registration requirements (amend Code Title 32 and add Code Chapter 17.110)

2026-175.headline: City Creates Cable Franchise Fund for Planning Bureau
2026-175.summary: The Bureau of Planning and Sustainability now has a dedicated fund to manage cable television revenues collected for public, educational, and government broadcasting. This change helps the bureau oversee local cable franchises and work with neighboring governments on shared media agreements.
2026-175.title: Authorize a Cable Franchise Fund for the Bureau of Planning and Sustainability to support the collection of Public, Education, and Government revenues and manage cable franchise work related to intergovernmental agreements with jurisdictions

2026-176.headline: City Code Updated to Remove Cable Regulatory Board
2026-176.summary: Portland updated its municipal code to remove references to the Mt. Hood Cable Regulatory Commission following the group's dissolution. The commission previously managed local cable television franchises and funded community technology grants across the region. Cable regulatory responsibilities and franchise management will now be handled directly by the city.
2026-176.title: Amend City Code to reflect the dissolution of the Mt. Hood Cable Regulatory Commission​ (amend Code Chapters 3.33 and 3.115)

2026-186.headline: Portland Creates Psychedelic Health and Safety Rules
2026-186.summary: Portland established a new city code governing psychedelic health and safety. The regulations set local guidelines and safety standards for the use and administration of psychedelic substances. These rules apply to service providers, businesses, and residents participating in regulated psychedelic programs within the city.
2026-186.title: Add Psychedelic Health and Safety Code (add Code Chapter 14B.140)

2026-189.headline: Portland Amends Land Use and Sign Regulations
2026-189.summary: Portland updated its zoning and sign regulations to streamline technical land use rules across the city. The changes clarify development standards, update definitions, and adjust guidelines for property owners and builders. These updates affect residents, local business owners, and land developers planning future construction projects.
2026-189.title: ​​Amend City Code and improve land use regulations through the Regulatory Improvement Code Amendment Package 11 (amend Code Titles 32 and 33)​

2026-192.headline: Portland Creates Resource Center for Ride-Hail Drivers
2026-192.summary: Rideshare drivers in Portland will have access to a new Drivers’ Resource Center to support their work. The city also updated traffic rules to clarify how local ride fees apply to services like Uber and Lyft. These changes affect rideshare drivers, transportation companies, and passengers.
2026-192.title: *Amend Vehicles and Traffic Code to clarify applicability of ride fees and establish a Drivers’ Resource Center for Transportation Network Company drivers (amend Code Sections 16.40.030 and 16.40.240)

2026-194.headline: Council Certifies Services to Secure State Funding
2026-194.summary: Portland confirmed it provides required municipal services, securing the city's eligibility for state tax revenues. This allows the city to receive its annual share of money collected by Oregon. The funding supports general city operations and local public services.
2026-194.title: Certify that certain services are provided by the City to establish eligibility for State Shared Revenues

2026-195.headline: Portland Accepts State Revenue Funds for 2026-27
2026-195.summary: Portland will accept state funding through Oregon's revenue sharing program for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. These funds support general city operations and public services for residents across the city. The money will help cover city expenses starting July 1, 2026.
2026-195.title: *Approve accepting funds from the State of Oregon under the State Revenue Sharing Program for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027

2026-196.headline: Portland Adopts FY 2026-2027 City Budget
2026-196.summary: Portland has established its official spending plan for the fiscal year running from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027. The budget allocates public funds for city services, staff, and public infrastructure projects. It affects all Portland residents and businesses that rely on city services or pay municipal taxes.
2026-196.title: Adopt the annual budget of the City and establish appropriations for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027

2026-197.headline: Portland Sets City Taxes for 2026-2027 Fiscal Year
2026-197.summary: Portland property taxes are established for the 2026-2027 fiscal year starting July 1, 2026. The tax revenues will fund general city services and operations over the twelve-month period. This tax levy applies to property owners living within Portland city limits.
2026-197.title: *Approve levying taxes for the City for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027

2026-198.headline: City Loans $600,000 from Parks to Hydroelectric Fund
2026-198.summary: Portland's Hydroelectric Power Operating Fund is receiving a temporary $600,000 loan from the Parks Capital Fund to cover short-term expenses. The transfer prevents the hydroelectric program from running a negative cash balance through the 2025-26 fiscal year-end. The borrowed money will be fully repaid to the city's parks capital account.
2026-198.title: *Authorize a temporary interfund loan not to exceed $600,000 from the Parks Capital Fund to the Hydroelectric Power Operating Fund to provide interim funding to avoid negative cash and fund balances at 2025-26 fiscal year-end

2026-199.headline: City Adjusts Funds in 2025-26 Supplemental Budget
2026-199.summary: Portland updated its 2025-26 city budget to cover over-spending across several city funds. These financial adjustments shift money between various municipal departments to balance operational costs. The changes affect how city departments manage their funding and spending for the remainder of the fiscal year.
2026-199.title: Adopt the Supplemental Budget for the FY 2025-26 over-expenditure process and make budget adjustments in various funds

2026-203.headline: City Restores Permitting Improvement Team
2026-203.summary: Portland is bringing back a specialized team to update and align the city's building and land-use rules. This second phase of the project focuses on making the city's permitting system clearer and more consistent. The changes will affect property owners, developers, and businesses applying for city permits.
2026-203.title: Direct the City Administrator to reestablish a Permitting Improvement Team to lead the second phase of the Code Alignment Project

2026-204.headline: Portland sets 2026 homebuyer tax exemption price cap
2026-204.summary: Portland established a maximum home sale price to qualify for the 2026 Homebuyer Opportunity Limited Tax Exemption program. The program provides a ten-year property tax exemption on structural improvements for qualifying buyers. This price cap determines which property purchases will be eligible for the tax break.
2026-204.title: Establish 2026 sale price cap for the Homebuyer Opportunity Limited Tax Exemption Program​

2026-205.headline: City Pauses Income Limits for Housing Fee Exemptions
2026-205.summary: Portland is temporarily removing buyer income requirements for homeownership developments seeking exemptions from city infrastructure fees. Developers building homes for sale can now receive these fee waivers without verifying the buyer's income level. This change affects residential home builders and prospective buyers across the city.
2026-205.title: Amend Partial and Full Exemptions of System Development Charges for Affordable Housing Developments Code to temporarily remove income requirements for homeownership units (amend Code Section 30.01.095)

2026-208.headline: Portland Appoints Clean Energy Board Members
2026-208.summary: New members will now help guide local climate and environmental funding decisions on the Portland Clean Energy Fund Committee. The fund provides grants for clean energy, energy efficiency, and job training programs in the city. This change affects Portland residents and community organizations applying for environmental project funding.
2026-208.title: ​​Appoint members to the Portland Clean Energy Community Benefits Fund Committee​

2026-209.headline: Portland Adds Funding Code for EV Charging Stations
2026-209.summary: Portland established a new city code section to create dedicated funding for electric vehicle charging stations. The rules outline how the city collects and spends money to build and maintain public charging infrastructure. This affects drivers, businesses, and city agencies involved in expanding electric vehicle access.
2026-209.title: Add Electric Vehicle Charging Systems Funding Code (add Code Chapter 26.11)

2026-210.headline: City Accepts Report on 2025 Council Agenda Items
2026-210.summary: Portland accepted formal recommendations reviewing how City Council agenda items were handled throughout 2025. The report tracks the final status of proposed city policies, ordinances, and council business. This document helps city staff and the public track the outcome of official items brought before the council.
2026-210.title: Accept recommendations in 2025 Agenda Item Disposition Report

2026-213.headline: Portland Restricts Turns on Red at High-Crash Streets
2026-213.summary: The Portland Bureau of Transportation will evaluate and restrict turns on red at traffic signals on streets with high crash rates. This change affects drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists using these intersections across the city.
2026-213.title: Direct the Portland Bureau of Transportation to evaluate and implement no turn on red restrictions at signalized intersections within the High Crash Network

2026-216.headline: Portland Extends Childcare Center Lease by 5 Years
2026-216.summary: The City of Portland is extending its lease for the CityKids Childcare and Development Center space for another five years. This agreement allows the facility to continue operating in its current location with Urban Office and Parking Facilities. The extension affects local families and staff who rely on the center for childcare services.
2026-216.title: Extend lease with Urban Office and Parking Facilities for the CityKids Childcare and Development Center space by five years (amend CLM Contract 10014)

2026-217.headline: Council Considers Appeals on Lloyd Center Master Plan
2026-217.summary: Community members and developers presented arguments regarding a long-term plan to redesign the Lloyd Center shopping mall property. The proposed master plan sets guidelines for future construction, public spaces, and land use in inner northeast Portland. The decision affects local business owners, nearby residents, and future development in the district.
2026-217.title: Consider appeals of the Design Commission’s approval of a voluntary Central City Master Plan Review and Adjustment Review for the Lloyd Center Central City Master Plan (LU 25-091308 CCMS AD)

2026-218.headline: City Revises Sewer and Stormwater Rates for 2026-27
2026-218.summary: Utility charges for Portland residents and businesses will change under updated sewer and stormwater rate schedules for the 2026-27 fiscal year. The adjusted fees determine how much property owners pay for city wastewater management and runoff services. The new rate structure will take effect during the upcoming budget period.
2026-218.title: *Revise sewer and stormwater rates, charges, and fees for FY 2026-27

2026-222.headline: Portland Allocates $18.9M to Restore Cut Frontline Jobs
2026-222.summary: Portland is reallocating nearly $19 million to restore frontline staff positions and public services that were previously cut from the city budget. Funding comes primarily from interest earned on the Portland Clean Energy Fund, along with other city and county resources. The money will also provide transition support for city employees affected by budget cuts.
2026-222.title: Amend the FY 2026-27 Budget to appropriate $13,076,892 in Portland Clean Energy Fund interest income, $5,491,002 other fund resources, and $335,000 in County IGA revenues to restore frontline positions and services reduced in the approved budget and to provide transition support for affected employees

2026-223.headline: City Adopts FY 2026-27 Supplemental Budget
2026-223.summary: Portland updated its 2026-27 budget to adjust city spending and manage financial risks to municipal services. The changes reallocate funds across city departments to help maintain existing public programs and services.
2026-223.title: Adopt a Supplemental Budget for FY 2026-27 to reduce potential risks to City services

2026-224.headline: Two Reappointed to Prosper Portland Board
2026-224.summary: Marcelino Alvarez and Eric Cress will continue serving on the Prosper Portland Board of Commissioners through September 5, 2029. The board oversees the city's economic development agency, which manages urban renewal projects and local business programs. Their leadership affects city investment strategies and economic growth initiatives across Portland.
2026-224.title: Reappoint Marcelino Alvarez and Eric Cress to the Prosper Portland Board of Commissioners for terms to expire September 5, 2029

2026-231.headline: Council Approves Meeting Records for May 2026
2026-231.summary: Official written records for city council meetings held between May 6 and May 27, 2026, are now finalized. These minutes serve as the formal public record of council discussions, votes, and decisions during that period. Portland residents can review these documents to track city government actions.
2026-231.title: Approve Council Minutes for May 6-27, 2026

2026-236.headline: Portland Leases Eastside Office for Safety Division
2026-236.summary: Portland's Community Safety Division is securing a new eastside office through a five-year lease with American Property Management. The agreement provides space for staff who coordinate local safety and emergency response programs. The move affects eastside residents accessing division services and city staff working in the area.
2026-236.title: *Authorize a five-year lease with American Property Management for Community Safety Division eastside office

2026-238.headline: Portland Utility Board Gains New Voting Members
2026-238.summary: New voting members are joining the Portland Utility Board to help oversee the city's water and sewer services. The community board advises city officials on utility rates, policies, and major bureau spending. This change impacts residents who rely on city water and wastewater systems.
2026-238.title: Appoint voting members to the Portland Utility Board

2026-241.headline: City Approves Premium Pay for Preschool Assistants
2026-241.summary: Preschool for All assistants and aides represented by LIUNA Local 483 will receive premium pay under a new labor agreement. The extra compensation applies to eligible staff working in the early childhood education program. This change updates wage terms for these unionized preschool support workers.
2026-241.title: *Authorize Letter of Agreement with the Laborers’ International Union of North America, Local 483 for premium pay to Assistants and Aides as defined in the Preschool for All Program

2026-242.headline: NW Portland Vacant Lot Rezoned for Parks Department
2026-242.summary: A vacant lot on NW 31st Avenue in Willamette Heights now has updated land use and zoning rules requested by Portland Parks and Recreation. The map changes allow the city parks department to officially manage the property under updated regulations. Nearby residents in Northwest Portland may see future park planning or development at the site.
2026-242.title: Amend the Comprehensive Plan Map and Zoning Map for a vacant lot on NW 31st Ave described as Willamette Heights Addition, Block 18, Lot 14 at the request of Portland Parks and Recreation (LU 26-007966 CP ZC)

2026-243.headline: City Renames Cesar E. Chavez Blvd to Campesinos Blvd
2026-243.summary: Cesar E. Chavez Boulevard will be renamed Campesinos Boulevard through a special exception to city street-naming rules. The change affects residents, property owners, and businesses along the corridor who must update address records. Emergency services and mapping tools will also transition to using the new street name.
2026-243.title: *Authorize exception to Code Chapter 17.93 Renaming City Streets and authorize the renaming of Cesar E. Chavez Blvd to Campesinos Blvd (allow exceptions to Code Sections 17.93.010, 17.93.020, 17.93.030, 17.93.040 and 17.93.050)

2026-247.headline: Portland Begins Foreclosure on 7545 NE Sandy Blvd
2026-247.summary: The City of Portland is moving forward with foreclosure on a property located at 7545 NE Sandy Blvd due to unpaid city liens. This step allows the city to recover delinquent debt owed by the property owner. If the unpaid balance is not resolved, the property may eventually be sold at auction.
2026-247.title: Initiate foreclosure action on 7545 NE Sandy Blvd for the collection of delinquent City Liens placed against the property

2026-248.headline: City Begins Foreclosure on NE Sandy Property
2026-248.summary: The City of Portland is starting foreclosure proceedings on a property located at 7545 NE Sandy Boulevard to collect unpaid city liens. This process allows the city to recover unpaid debt owed by the property owner. If the debt remains unpaid, the property may be sold through a court process.
2026-248.title: Initiate foreclosure action on 7545 WI/NE Sandy Blvd for the collection of delinquent City Liens placed against the property

2026-250.headline: City Begins Foreclosure on N Columbia Blvd Property
2026-250.summary: Portland is initiating foreclosure on a North Columbia Boulevard property to collect unpaid city liens. The action allows the city to claim or sell the site to recover unpaid debts. It directly impacts the property owner while enforcing local debt collection policies.
2026-250.title: Initiate foreclosure action on N Columbia Blvd for the collection of delinquent City Liens placed against the property

2026-253.headline: City Starts Foreclosure on SE Division Street Property
2026-253.summary: The city is starting a foreclosure process on a property located at 7101–7103 SE Division Street to collect unpaid city liens. This step allows the city to recover delinquent fees owed by the owner. The action directly affects the property owner and any current occupants.
2026-253.title: Initiate foreclosure action on 7101–7103 SE Division St for the collection of delinquent City Liens placed against the property

2026-256.headline: City Initiates Foreclosure on NE Alberta Street Property
2026-256.summary: The City of Portland is beginning foreclosure proceedings against a commercial property located at 2734-2738 NE Alberta Street. The action allows the city to collect overdue funds from unpaid liens placed on the address. This change affects the property owner and enables the city to recover outstanding debts.
2026-256.title: Initiate foreclosure action on 2734-2738 NE Alberta St for the collection of delinquent City Liens placed against the property

2026-260.headline: City Begins Foreclosure on SE Lambert Street Home
2026-260.summary: Portland is initiating foreclosure on the property at 5706 SE Lambert St to collect unpaid city liens. This process allows the city to recover debts owed for unpaid municipal fees and assessments. If the outstanding balance is not paid, the property may be sold at auction.
2026-260.title: Initiate foreclosure action on 5706 SE Lambert St for the collection of delinquent City Liens placed against the property

2026-267.headline: City Pays $287,500 Settlement for Water Bureau Crash
2026-267.summary: The City of Portland will pay $287,500 to settle a lawsuit over a collision involving a Portland Water Bureau dump truck. The payment resolves claims made by an individual for bodily injuries suffered in the crash.
2026-267.title: *Pay settlement of Michael Duffer bodily injury lawsuit in the sum of $287,500 resulting from a collision with a City dump truck involving the Portland Water Bureau

2026-270.headline: Portland Advances New PSU Arts Center and Keller Plans
2026-270.summary: Portland is moving forward with plans for a new performing arts venue at Portland State University capable of hosting Broadway shows. The city will also begin planning for the future of the historic Keller Auditorium. These steps affect local arts groups, downtown visitors, and the university community.
2026-270.title: Accept the Future of Large-Scale Performing Arts recommendations to advance a new Broadway-capable venue as part of the proposed Performing Arts + Culture Center at Portland State University, and initiate planning for the future of the Keller Auditorium

2026-272.headline: City Allocates $35 Million in Federal Loan Funds
2026-272.summary: Portland is adding $35 million in federal funding to support local community development projects. These funds will allow organizations to access lower-cost loans for housing and economic development across the city. The program provides financing to help build infrastructure and expand local services.
2026-272.title: Appropriate grant award of $35 million for Section 108 Loan Guarantee Program

2026-277.headline: City accepts $207K grant to curb street racing
2026-277.summary: Portland is accepting $207,411 in grant funding to address illegal street racing and street takeovers. The money will support targeted law enforcement patrols and enforcement efforts across the city. This affects drivers and residents living in neighborhoods impacted by street takeovers.
2026-277.title: *Appropriate grant award of $207,411 for speed racing street takeover

2026-278.headline: City Accepts $103,069 Grant for Traffic Enforcement
2026-278.summary: Portland will use a $103,069 grant to increase traffic enforcement patrols across the city. The funds will pay for officer overtime focused on traffic safety and law enforcement. This change affects drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians traveling on local streets.
2026-278.title: *Appropriate grant award of $103,069 for expanded traffic enforcement

2026-280.headline: City approves terms for Moda Center arena renovation
2026-280.summary: A new non-binding framework sets initial terms for major renovations at the Moda Center arena. The agreement aims to keep the Portland Trail Blazers playing in the city for at least another 20 years. It establishes guidelines for future operating and lease contracts between the city and team management.
2026-280.title: Authorize a non-binding term sheet with Rip City Management LLC and Trail Blazers Holdings, LLC outlining the terms for Moda Center arena renovation, operating and lease agreements that will keep the Portland Trail Blazers playing in Portland for at least 20 more years

2026-285.headline: City Seeks Partner to Develop Moda Center Land
2026-285.summary: Portland is beginning a search for a partner to build on city-owned land near the Moda Center. The city administrator will create a process to select a developer for these Rose Quarter properties. This move sets the stage for future construction and revitalization around the arena.
2026-285.title: Direct the City Administrator to advance a process to identify a development partner for City-owned properties adjacent to the Moda Center

2026-289.headline: City Appoints New Portlanders Policy Commissioners
2026-289.summary: New members were appointed to the New Portlanders Policy Commission for terms starting in September 2026. This advisory body helps guide city decisions on issues affecting immigrant and refugee communities. The appointments fill upcoming vacancies on the civic board.
2026-289.title: Appoint members to the New Portlanders Policy Commission for terms beginning September 2, 2026

2026-294.headline: City to Subsidize Transit Passes for Employees
2026-294.summary: A new pilot program will subsidize public transit passes for Portland city employees. Funding for the program comes from an increase of up to $245,000 in city bureau rates for the 2026-27 fiscal year. The decision affects municipal workers and city bureau budgets.
2026-294.title: *Authorize an increase up to $245,000 in bureau rates for FY 2026-27 to implement a pilot program to subsidize transit passes for City employees

2026-299.headline: Council Urges Transparency in Data Center Agreements
2026-299.summary: Portland's City Administrator is asked to stop signing non-disclosure agreements regarding potential data center projects. The administrator must now inform City Council about inquiries from data center developers and involve the public in future deal reviews. This affects how technology companies negotiate with the city and gives residents earlier notice of proposed developments.
2026-299.title: Urge the City Administrator to refrain from signing data center non-disclosure agreements, notify City Council of inquiries for data center deals, and engage in transparent public processes related to data centers

2026-306.headline: City creates new Council Public Information Officer job
2026-306.summary: Portland established a new non-union staff position for a Council Public Information Officer. The role includes a newly defined salary range to manage public communications for the City Council. This change affects city administrative hiring and staff structure.
2026-306.title: Create new non-represented classification of Council Public Information Officer and establish a compensation range for this classification

2026-307.headline: Portland Creates New Data and Privacy Officer Role
2026-307.summary: Portland created a new management position for a City Data and Privacy Officer and set its pay range. The official will oversee how the city handles public data and protects resident privacy. This change updates city job classifications and establishes leadership for municipal data policies.
2026-307.title: Create new non-represented classification of City Data and Privacy Officer and establish a compensation range for this classification

2026-310.headline: Omar Salomon Appointed to Homelessness Oversight Committee
2026-310.summary: Omar K. Salomon will join the Steering and Oversight Committee for the Homelessness Response System. The committee helps guide local policies and programs aimed at addressing homelessness. Salomon will serve in this advisory role through September 30, 2027.
2026-310.title: Appoint Omar K. Salomon to the Steering and Oversight Committee for the Homelessness Response System for a one-year term to expire September 30, 2027

2026-320.headline: City Council Approves Summer 2026 Meeting Minutes
2026-320.summary: Official written records for Portland City Council meetings held between June 3 and July 30, 2026, are now formally adopted. These public records document the council's discussions, votes, and official actions during that period. Residents can access these published minutes to review past city decisions.
2026-320.title: Approve Council Minutes for June 3 - July 30, 2026

2026-339.headline: City Settles Bicycle Crash Lawsuit for $125,000
2026-339.summary: The City of Portland will pay $125,000 to settle a lawsuit with a cyclist injured in a crash involving the Portland Bureau of Transportation. The payment covers bodily injuries sustained by Joseph Rios during the incident. This agreement resolves all legal claims against the city related to the crash.
2026-339.title: *Pay settlement of Joseph Rios bodily injury lawsuit in the sum of $125,000 resulting from a bicycle crash involving Portland Bureau of Transportation
